MODULE 1: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### 3-ON-2 CONVERT THE ADVANTAGE

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide players into groups of seven at all available baskets. Three players will start on offense with two players on defense (and two defenders off to the baseline). The offense must score a 3PT shot or a lay-up in 10 seconds (we will call these 'bursts'). The offense will complete six 'bursts' against the defense with different defensive combinations rotating in each time. Players should start 'bursts' quickly and from different locations on the floor. After six 'bursts', a new group will become the offense.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover). The team (offense or defense) with the most points wins. If there is a tie, play an additional 'burst'.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Identifying ROB shots (Range, Open, Balance)
- Making quick decisions to increase the advantage
- Identifying matchup advantages

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- Escape the lava. After a pass or cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out). If they are still inside the lava after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Simply convert the 3-on-2 advantage which exists.
- Create a 3-on-2+1 with the offense starting with a blind advantage. If the advantage is lost and the defense recovers and matches up with the offense, it is an instant turnover.
- If there is a coach at each basket, the offense can clear the ball by passing to the coach to start the next 'burst'. Coaches can increase the pace and vary starting locations.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players understand the 'bursts' concept.
- Ensure that the defenders secure the made or missed shot before rotating off to wait for their next turn.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Was your shot a ROB Shot? If not, what was missing?"
- "In what ways can the defenders disrupt the offense?"
- "Is it possible to overpass?"
- "What are your matchup advantages?"

Load for younger players

MODULE 1: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### 5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED

24 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of five players, based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get a point. The losing team rotates off while the next team waiting rotates on defense at the opposite end. The team that gets a point gets to maintain possession and stay on offense. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

#### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Taking advantage of scramble situations
- Transitioning with speed and pace (offense and defense)
- Maintaining balanced spacing while moving off-ball (cuts, screens, etc.)

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you get the most efficient shot?"
- "What can you do to space the floor effectively?"

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, play 4-on-4, with a +1 who is always on offense.
- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- Escape the lava. After a pass or cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out outside the 3PT line). If they are still inside after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Players can only create an advantage through a static 1-on-1 where the ball-handler creates an advantage with a dribble move from the perimeter, or through a post-up. Teammates should maintain spacing (following the 'lava' load), ready to receive the ball.
- A score within five seconds of gaining the ball on defense is worth double the points.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Organize the waiting teams on the sideline so teams transition quickly for the next repetition.
- Ensure players substitute every few minutes.
- Help players look to advance the ball by finding open players.

MODULE 1: FULL OUTLINE

FINAL BUZZER

Basketball School

## FINAL BUZZER

is our closing huddle where coaches see the players off as a group. The Final Buzzer should take no more than 5 minutes to maximize player's attention spans. There are five parts that should be covered in every Final Buzzer:

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

CONCLUSION

Players are debriefed on the learnings and prepared for the end of the module.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together! "NBA Basketball School on 3! (Location Name) on 6!"

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

COMMENCEMENT

Players are primed and prepped for the start of the camp.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together! "NBA Basketball School on 3! (Location Name) on 6!"
